title: Artificial Intelligence Powered Morphology Characterization for Advanced Material Design and Failure Analysis
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown to be valuable in various disciplines, ranging from medicine to scientific research etc. [1-2]. In principle AI may be divided, into predictive and generative AI models. Predictive AI models combine statistical analysis with machine learning algorithms, with the ability to make predictions about most likely results. Here, for instance deep learning-based concepts can be utilized for the semantic segmentation of image data. This has been shown in medicine but also in material science and failure analysis in particular for tomography-based imaging methods but also for large two-dimensional image data sets [3,4]. Generative AI on the other hand is able to create content, based on patterns and relationships drawn from the delivered training data. In comparison to predictive algorithms, generative ones are able to create. Examples for generative AI algorithm comprise for instance large language models (LLMs), generative adversarial networks (GANs) or denoised diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) etc. [5-8].
